3.  Findings to Continue to Hold Remote TeleconferenceNirtual City Council Meetings
  Pursuant to Assembly Bill 361
  As the State of Emergency has ended, the City Council can continue to hold virtual
  meetings without providing notice of the City Council’s teleconference location if the City
  Council makes the following two findings: 1. State or local officials have imposed or
  recommended measures to promote social distancing in connection with COVID-19; and
  2. The City Council reconsiders the circumstances of the state of the emergency and
  danger presented by COVID-19; Having made the findings, the City Council can continue
  every 30 days to authorize meetings under AR 261 to protect the health or safety of
  attendees.

  Recommended Action
  Reconsider the circumstances of COVID-19 state of emergency proclaimed by the
  Governor and COVID-19’s continued impact and determine that state or local officials
  have imposed or recommended measures to promote social distancing in connection with
  COVID-19, and as such, that continuing to utilize the protections of Assembly Bill 361 will
  protect the health and safely of attendees.

4.  League of California Cities Annual Voting Delegate
  The Annual League of California Cities Conference will be held in Sacramento, California
  from September 20 to 22, 2023. At the business meeting, the League membership
  considers and takes action on resolutions that establish League Policy. In order to vote
  at the Business Meeting, City Council must designate a voting delegate and an alternate
  voting delegate.
  Recommended Action
  Adopt a resolution appointing Mayor Marshall as the voting delegate and Mayor Pro Tern
  Michael Ponce as an alternate delegate voting for the Annual League of California Cities
  Conference in September 2023.

5.  Declare Old Vehicles and Equipment as Surplus
  Staff has compiled a list of vehicles that the City of Avalon (City”) no longer uses and are
  insufficient for the current needs. Historically, the City Council is presented with a list of
  items that are surplus, the Council declares it surplus, and then the declared items are
  either sold via Public Surplus, given to charity, or disposed of properly.
  Recommended Action
  Adopt a resolution declaring vehicles and equipment listed in resolution as surplus
  property and authorize the City Manager to dispose of it in accordance with City policy.

6.  Authorize Purchase of a 2016 Ford F-250 Pickup Truck for the Wastewater Treatment
  Plant
  Public Works and PERC are requesting to procure a used 2016 Ford F-250 pickup truck
  to replace an existing truck.
  Recommended Action
  Authorize the City Manager or designee to procure, per the City’s Purchasing Policy, a
  used 2016 Ford F-250 pickup truck from United Rentals for the Wastewater Treatment
  Plant. Allocate $28,500 from the vehicle replacement fund (account 13825-6781) to
  procure the vehicle.

7.  Electronic Signature Policy
  The City desires to implement industry best practices of using electronic records and
  electronic signatures to effectively manage documents in accordance with California state
  law. It is recommended City Council formally authorize the use of electronic signatures
  for the execution of City business.
  Recommended Action
  Approve the City of Avalon Electronic Signature Policy.

8.  Avalon Mooring and Diving Service: Inc. Contract Extension
  The Avalon Mooring & Diving Service has been contracted to provide mooring
  maintenance services in Avalon since July 1, 1994. The initial contract agreement was
  for a five year term — expiring on June 30, 1999. The contract has been extended by
  amendment six (6) times, each time for a five-year term. The sixth amendment to the
  contract agreement expired on June 30, 2023. The City received a request from Avalon
  Mooring Services, Inc. to extend the contract for an additional five-year term on July 11.
  2023. The proposed new term would expire on June 30, 2028.
  Recommended Action
  Authorize the City Manager to execute a seventh amendment extending the franchise
  agreement with Avalon Mooring & Diving Service, Inc., for an additional five (5) years
  from July 1, 2023 to June 30, 2028.

SUBJECT:  Findings to Continue to Hold Remote TeleconferenceNirtual City

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Reconsider the circumstances of COVID-1 9 state of emergency
proclaimed by the Governor and COVID-1 9’s continued impact and determine that state or local
officials have imposed or recommended measures to promote social distancing in connection
with COVID-19, and as such, that continuing to utilize the protections of Assembly Bill 361 will
protect the health and safely of attendees.

REPORT SUMMARY: Traditionally, the Brown Act allows for teleconference or virtual meetings,
provided that the physical locations of the legislative body’s members joining by teleconference
are posted on the agenda, that those locations are open to the public and that a quorum of the
members is located within its jurisdiction. AS 361 provides an exception to these procedures in
order to allow for fully virtual meetings during proclaimed emergencies, including the COVID-19
pandemic.

Since March of 2020 and the issuance of Governor Newsom’s Executive Order N-29-20, which
suspended portions of the Brown Act relating to teleconferencing, the City Council has had virtual
meetings without having to post the location of the legislative body members attending virtually.
Most public agencies have been holding public meetings using virtual platforms since this time.
In June of 2021, Governor Newsom issued Executive Order N-08-21, which provided that the
exceptions contained in EO N-29-20 would sunset on September 30, 2021.

On September 10, 2021, the Legislature adopted AS 361, which allows public agencies to hold
fully virtual meetings under certain circumstances without the posting of the agenda from each
location a legislative body member is attending. Governor Newsom signed the bill into law on
September 16, 2021. Because it contained an urgency provision, it took immediate effect.

Specific Findings Required underAB 361

As the State of Emergency has ended, the City Council can continue to hold virtual meetings
without providing notice of the City Council’s teleconference location if the City Council makes
the following two findings:

  1. State or local officials have imposed or recommended measures to promote social
  distancing in connection with COVID-19; and

  2. The City Council reconsiders the circumstances of the state of the emergency and danger
  presented by COVID-19;

  CITY OF AVALON
  Electronic Signature Policy

APPLICABILITY
This Policy applies to all City of Avalon (“City”) employees, officers, and designated contractors
who, as part of their job responsibilities and requirements are tasked with executing legally-
binding documents. The use of electronic signatures on legally-binding documents has become
increasingly prevalent. The benefits of electronic signatures are simple and numerous: they cut
down on the paper, time and cost associated with transmitting and approving physical
documents, and can offer an easily accessible audit trail of the modification, editing, approval,
and signature of documents.

STATEMENT OF PURPOSE
This Policy authorizes the City to accept an approved electronic signature, in lieu of a written
signature, on a document in which a signature is required or used, which complies with the
requirements of Government Code section 16.5 and this Policy. This Policy does not supersede
laws that specifically require a written signature. This Policy does not limit the right or option to
conduct the transaction on paper or in non-electronic form and the right to have documents
provided on paper.

DEFINITIONS
An electronic signature means an electric sound, symbol, or process attached to or logically
associated with an electronic record and executed or adopted by a person with the intent to sign
the electronic record.

A “digital signature” is a type of electronic signature that shall have the same force and effect as a
manual signature if and only if it embodies the following attributes pursuant to Government
Code § 16.5:
  •  It is unique to the person using it;
  •  It is capable of verification;
  •  It is under the sole control of the person using it;
  •  It is linked to data in such a manner that if the data are changed, the digital signature is
  invalidated; and
  •  It conforms to regulations adopted by the Secretary of State.

GENERAL POLICY GUIDELINES
  1. In any document accepted by the City in which a signature is required or used, the City

  3. The final approval of any electronic signature method will be by the City Manager and City

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S):  Authorize the City Manager to execute a seventh
amendment extending the franchise agreement with Avalon Mooring & Diving Service, Inc., for
an additional five (5) years from July 1, 2023 to June 30, 2028.

REPORT SUMMARY: The Avalon Mooring & Diving Service has been contracted to provide
mooring maintenance services in Avalon since July 1, 1994.

The initial contract agreement was for a five year term  expiring on June 30, 1999. The
  —

contract has been extended by amendment six (6) times, each time for a five-year term.

The sixth amendment to the contract agreement expired on June 30, 2023. The City received
a request from Avalon Mooring Services, Inc. to extend the contract for an additional five-year
term on July 11, 2023. The proposed new term would expire on June 30, 2028.

For the term of this renewal, Avalon Mooring Service is requesting they be allowed to adjust
rates annually according to the CPI and California State Sales Tax rate fluctuations.

Per the Avalon Municipal Code:

Sec. 10-2.411 Franchises for Mooring Services.

  No person, other than an owner or lessee thereof, may repair, replace, renovate,
construct, install or otherwise service moorings in City waters without first having obtained a
franchise therefore from the City. This franchise shall be in addition to any business license
otherwise required by this Code, but shall satisfy the waterside project permit requirement of
Section 4-2.4 10.

  Applications for mooring service franchises shall be submitted on forms provided by the
City containing such information as is required by the City Manager The City Council may
grant a franchise for mooring services, if upon review of the application, the Council makes the
following affirmative findings:

  (a)  The applicant will operate the mooring service on a twenty-four (24) hours per
day basis for twelve (12) n7onths a year
   (b)  The applicant demonstrates the financial capability, skills, qualifications and
facilities properly to perform mooring services.

  (c)  The applicant has presented facts demonstrating a need for operation of the
proposed business in City waters.

  (d)  The proposed business will not have a deleterious impact on the public health,
safety and welfare.

  The term of any such franchise shall not exceed five (5) years. The franchise shall enter
into a franchise agreement with the City which sets forth the terms and conditions of operation
of such service, including a franchise fee to be paid to the City.
(2, Ord. 736, eff April 14, 1983; §2, Ord. 872-92, eff. April 2, 1992)

issuing an REP would result in better service or lower prices.
